one_line: AI spending climbs, regulators act, and security incidents highlight sector challenges.

themes.title: AI infrastructure spending surges
themes.text: Big tech firms disclosed over $3 trillion in data‑center commitments, while investors reacted to $800 billion‑plus AI capex, causing stock declines. Companies such as AM Intelligence and Runware are raising billions to fund Nvidia hardware and mass‑produce AI pods, and Fujifilm is expanding tape production for generative‑AI workloads.

stories.headline: Big tech firms commit over $3 trillion to AI data‑center spending
US tech stocks tumble as AI spending approaches $1 trillion
Big tech AI capex sparks cash‑flow concerns, stocks tumble
AM Intelligence seeks up to $3 billion to fund Nvidia Vera Rubin chip purchase
Runware plans factory to mass‑produce AI pods at car‑assembly line speed
Fujifilm to boost magnetic tape production fivefold as AI drives data archiving

themes.title: Regulators shape AI data rules
themes.text: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic adopted a shared robots.txt opt‑out signal, and OpenAI pledged to honor it. The UK High Court upheld Ofcom’s data‑request notices, the Competition and Markets Authority opened a probe into Meta’s publisher terms, and India’s TRAI issued draft AI governance guidelines. OpenAI also expanded safety safeguards for teen users and violence‑related content.

stories.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic adopt shared robots.txt opt‑out standard
OpenAI says it will honor robots.txt signal for AI training preferences
UK high court rejects Meta, TikTok and X challenge to Ofcom data requests
UK competition regulator probes Meta's terms for publishers and advertisers
TRAI drafts AI policy framework requiring board approval and incident reporting for telecoms
OpenAI tightens weapons‑related information limits for teen ChatGPT users
OpenAI adds expanded safeguards to ChatGPT for violence prevention

themes.title: AI tools exploited in attacks
themes.text: Chinese state‑linked hackers used the DeepSeek model via the ARTEX framework to breach over 200 organizations in multiple countries. A malicious version of Anthropic’s Claude Code VS Code extension attempted to install a persistent SSH backdoor, potentially affecting up to 5,000 users.

stories.headline: China‑linked hackers used DeepSeek AI via ARTEX to breach 200+ firms in 11 days
Malicious Claude Code VS Code extension adds SSH backdoor, affecting up to 5,000 users
